hero.title: Compress a video to 25 MB
hero.lead: 25 MB is the cap on Gmail and Outlook attachments and Discord's classic Nitro limit. It holds roughly a minute of full-HD video, or about twenty minutes if you accept a small, soft picture. Drop your video below and it's compressed to just under 25 MB on your own device — no upload, no account, no watermark.
answer.h2: How long is 25 MB of video?
answer.lead: There's no single answer, because it's a trade between length and picture quality: the longer the clip, the less detail fits in the same 25 MB. The table below is what this compressor actually produces from a typical phone recording — full HD, 30 frames a second, with sound.

answer.r3.q: Clearly reduced — fine on a phone, soft on a laptop

answer.after: Past about 20 minutes, 25 MB stops being enough for a picture worth watching. Rather than hand you mush, the compressor refuses and tells you the smallest size that would actually work for your clip. For an exact figure before you start, the bitrate calculator does the sum for your own video's length and resolution.
prose.h2: Why 25 MB, and what to expect
prose.p1: Gmail and Outlook both cap attachments at 25 MB, and Discord's Nitro Basic tier uses the same limit. Most services check the exact byte count, so a "25.1 MB" file bounces. This tool always lands under the limit: it works out exactly how much to compress so the video fits, leaves room for the audio, then checks the result and compresses again if the first pass came out a touch too big. You'll typically get a file between 22 and 25 MB — never over.
prose.p2: Where the quality goes is worth knowing in advance. Rather than smearing every frame equally, the compressor keeps the picture sharp and shrinks its dimensions instead — so a long video comes back clear but physically smaller, not blurry at full size. Below a certain point it also drops the frame rate. That's why the table above talks about picture size rather than a quality percentage. All of it runs locally in your browser, so a 300 MB source doesn't need a 300 MB upload before work even starts.
faq.q1: Will the file really be under 25 MB?
faq.a1: Yes. The tool checks the final size and automatically compresses a little more if needed. It never hands you a file over the target.
faq.q2: Is the video uploaded to a server?
faq.a2: No. Compression happens in your browser on your own device. There is no upload and no server-side processing — which is also why it's fast and free.
faq.q3: Why does Gmail still reject my 25 MB file?
faq.a3: Email encodes attachments in a format that adds roughly 33% overhead, so Gmail's effective limit for attachments is lower than 25 MB of file. If your compressed file is close to 25 MB and still bounces, compress to a custom target of 18 MB on the generic compressor instead.
faq.a4: On a typical laptop in Chrome, faster than the video's own duration — a 4-minute video compresses in under 4 minutes, usually much less, because it uses your device's own video hardware.
faq.q5: Can I pick a different size?
faq.a5: Yes — use the full compressor, which has 8, 10, 16, 25 and 50 MB presets plus a custom field.
faq.q6: How many seconds of video is 25 MB?
faq.a6: At full HD, roughly 60 to 90 seconds. Drop to a smaller picture and the same 25 MB stretches much further — around five minutes at a reduced size, or twenty minutes at a small one. Quality is what you're trading, not time.
faq.q7: Is 25 MB enough for a 10-minute video?
faq.a7: Yes, but the picture will be noticeably small — fine on a phone, blocky on a TV. Around 20 minutes is the practical ceiling; beyond that the compressor will tell you the smallest size that still gives a watchable result.
